exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Music Preferences
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What kind of music do you like, Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I really like hip-hop. The strong beat makes me want to move.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see. For me it's classical music. It makes me feel calm and peaceful.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Calm? When do you usually listen to it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: When I'm studying. It helps me concentrate. What about you?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I play hip-hop when I exercise, because it gives me energy.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That makes sense. Different music for different moods.

exercises.translation_cn: Anna 问 Tom 喜欢什么音乐;Tom 喜欢嘻哈,强节拍让他想动;Anna 喜欢古典乐,让她平静;她学习时听以助专注;Tom 锻炼时放嘻哈来提神;两人都觉得不同心情配不同音乐。

questions.stem: What kind of music does Tom like?
Why does Tom like that music?
options: Its strong beat makes him want to move.

questions.stem: How does classical music make Anna feel?
When does Anna usually listen to her favourite music?
Why does Tom play his music while exercising?
options: It is required by the gym.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 The School Music Festival
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Good morning, everyone. Our school music festival will be held next month on the sports field.
The aim of the festival is to raise money for charity.
Anyone who can sing or play an instrument may try out as a performer.
Students who think they have no musical talent can still help in other ways.
You can sell tickets, run a food stand, or set up the equipment before the show.
exercises.translation_cn: 通知:校园音乐节将于下月在运动场举办;目的是为慈善筹款;会唱歌或演奏乐器的人都可报名当表演者;觉得自己没有音乐天赋的同学也能帮忙;可以卖票、经营食品摊,或在演出前架设设备。

questions.stem: Where will the music festival be held?
What is the aim of the festival?
Who can try out as a performer?
options: Anyone who can sing or play an instrument.

questions.stem: What can students without musical talent do?
options: Help with tickets, food or equipment.

questions.stem: Which task is mentioned for volunteers?

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Learning the Guitar
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: I'm really struggling with the guitar. My fingers just won't move fast enough.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Don't worry. Real progress is gradual; nobody plays well after one week.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: So what should I do?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Try practising a little every day instead of one long session.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: That's a good idea. Anything else?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Record yourself playing, then listen and find your mistakes.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: I see. So I can hear what to fix.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Exactly. Little by little, you'll get much better.

exercises.translation_cn: Ben 学吉他很吃力,手指不够快;Mia 说进步是渐进的,没人一周就弹好;建议每天练一点,而非一次练很久;还建议录下自己演奏再听、找出错误;一点点就会进步很多。

questions.stem: What problem does Ben have?
options: His fingers won't move fast enough on the guitar.

questions.stem: What does Mia say about progress?
options: It is gradual and takes time.

questions.stem: What is Mia's first piece of advice?
What is Mia's second piece of advice?
What does Mia promise will happen little by little?

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 What a Virtual Choir Is
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A virtual choir lets people sing together even when they are far apart.
Each member records a video of themselves singing alone at home.
All the videos are uploaded and joined into one performance online.
Anyone with a camera and the Internet can take part, from anywhere.
In this way, a virtual choir connects ordinary people into one global community.
exercises.translation_cn: 虚拟合唱团让相隔甚远的人也能一起唱;每位成员在家独自录下唱歌的视频;所有视频被上传并合成一段网络演出;任何有摄像头和网络的人都能参加;这样虚拟合唱团把普通人联结成一个全球社区。

questions.stem: What does a virtual choir let people do?
options: Sing together even when far apart.

questions.stem: How does each member take part?
options: By singing on a real stage.
By recording a video alone at home.

questions.stem: What happens to all the videos?
options: They are joined into one online performance.

questions.stem: Who can take part in a virtual choir?
options: Anyone with a camera and the Internet.

questions.stem: What does a virtual choir connect ordinary people into?

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Choosing an Instrument
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: I'd like to learn an instrument, but I can't decide which one.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Do you prefer a stringed instrument or a wind instrument?

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: What's the difference exactly?

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: A stringed instrument, like the violin, makes sound from its strings. A wind one, like the flute, needs air.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: I think I'd rather try something with strings.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Then how about the guitar? It's a good choice for a beginner.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Great idea. I'll start with the guitar.

exercises.translation_cn: Lucy 想学乐器但拿不定主意;Sam 问她偏好弦乐还是管乐;Lucy 问两者区别;Sam 解释弦乐(如小提琴)靠琴弦发声,管乐(如长笛)靠空气;Lucy 更想试弦乐;Sam 建议吉他适合初学者;Lucy 决定从吉他学起。

questions.stem: What is Lucy's problem at the start?
options: She can't decide which instrument to learn.

questions.stem: How does a stringed instrument make sound?
options: By being struck like a drum.

questions.stem: What kind of instrument is the flute, according to Sam?
Which kind does Lucy prefer to try?
Which instrument does Lucy finally choose?

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Music and Your Mood
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple idea for anyone who feels tired or sad.
Try letting music change your mood for a few minutes.
A happy song can give you energy when you feel low.
A quiet piece can bring you relief after a hard day.
Whatever you are feeling, the right music can somehow make it a little better.
exercises.translation_cn: 给感到疲惫或难过的人一个小建议:试着让音乐花几分钟改变你的心情;低落时,一首欢快的歌能给你能量;辛苦一天后,一段安静的曲子能带来宽慰;无论你有什么感受,合适的音乐总能让它变好一些。

questions.stem: Who is this idea for?
options: Anyone who feels tired or sad.

questions.stem: What can a happy song do when you feel low?
What can a quiet piece bring after a hard day?
How long does the speaker suggest letting music change your mood?
What is the speaker's main message?
options: Music is a waste of time.
You should never listen to music.
The right music can somehow make your mood better.
